title: Nvidia Is Hiring Someone to Market to Agents
summary: Nvidia is hiring a Director of Agent Marketing, and the job description names the audience out loud. Versions of this role will spread until marketing to agents is simply called marketing.
body_markdown:
Nvidia is hiring a[Director of Agent Marketing](https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite/job/US-CA-Santa-Clara/Director--Agent-Marketing_JR2020660) . The posting is live as I write this: Santa Clara, base salary between $224,000 and $339,250, reporting into the VP of Global Digital Marketing. The job description's second paragraph opens with a sentence I would frame: "Marketing now has two audiences: People, and the AI agents they ask for answers."


Read the title the way you would read any marketing title. In developer marketing, the developer is the audience. In enterprise marketing, the enterprise is the audience. Agent marketing is marketing to agents. The software is the audience, and the job exists to make Nvidia "found, cited, recommended, and chosen by AI-powered discovery."


### The audience formed before the job did


We argued in[AI Is a New Audience for Brands](https://www.unusual.ai/blog/ai-is-a-new-audience-for-brands) that this audience had already formed whether or not anyone was assigned to it, and in[The Newest Job in Marketing: AI Psychologist](https://www.unusual.ai/blog/the-newest-job-in-marketing-ai-psychologist) that someone would eventually own it as a title. Job titles are lagging indicators. By the time a director-level job description gets written, the budget conversation has already happened and someone senior has already argued this is a function and won.


It makes sense that this lands in B2B first. B2B buying runs on specs, price, integration surface, and proof, exactly the dimensions a machine reader compares well. The buyer that reads every spec sheet without fatigue is the buyer B2B products were accidentally designed for.


### The title aims higher than the job description


There is a gap worth naming between the title and the tasks. The job description asks the hire to lead "AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)" and boost citation frequency across AI platforms. We wrote about why[AEO and GEO are horseless carriages](https://www.unusual.ai/blog/aeo-and-geo-are-horseless-carriages) : citation rate counts appearances and says nothing about whether the model, having read everything, would recommend you to a buyer with real constraints. It is the same confusion[the Wall Street Journal made about AI search](https://www.unusual.ai/blog/ai-search-is-already-dying) , describing something fundamentally new in the previous era's vocabulary.


The title speaks to the higher aspiration. "Agent marketing" names the audience correctly, and phrases like "answer quality" circle the real work: knowing what the models believe about you and moving those beliefs with evidence.


### There will be more of these


Functions propagate through org charts. A peer CMO sees the posting, forwards it with "do we have this?", and a quarter later the title exists in three more places. Growth marketing spread this way, and developer relations did too. So the useful exercise is to answer the forwarded question honestly: who owns the agent audience at your company today? Who knows what ChatGPT tells a qualified buyer about your pricing? At most companies the honest answer is nobody, and the audience is being marketed to anyway, by whatever the models happened to read.


Follow the trend far enough and the title dissolves into the department. When the agent is the audience that decides what reaches the buyer, marketing to agents stops being a specialty. It is just marketing. Nvidia priced the head start at roughly $300,000 a year.
